alarm_summary.recent_fix: Pressure sensor replaced on chamber B on 2026-11-01 11:00. No repair is recorded for chamber A in the last 30 days.
alarm_summary.recent_alarm: A-1052 on chamber A on 2026-11-13 07:55. Before that, A-1023 on chambers A and B on 2026-11-11. A-1023 also occurred on chamber B on 2026-11-01 and 2026-11-03.

likely_causes: Chamber A temperature sensor reading is wrong or has drifted. This is the first thing SOP-020 checks against the backup sensor.
Chiller setpoint is wrong or coolant flow is reduced, so the chamber is not cooled enough.
Heater power output is too high or faulty, which pushes the temperature above the upper limit.
ETCH-03 has had several other alarms in the last 7 days (A-1023 and A-1052). These may point to a shared underlying problem on the tool, but nothing found links them to A-1031.
A-1031 has not been reported on ETCH-03 in the last 30 days. It was reported on ETCH-05 (3 times) and ETCH-07 (once), so a common cause across tools is possible but not confirmed.

alarm_summary.recent_fix: None. ETCH-09 had no repairs in the last 90 days.
alarm_summary.recent_alarm: None. ETCH-09 had no alarms in the last 90 days, and no tool reported A-1042 in the last 30 days.

likely_causes: Mass flow controller drift or a setpoint mismatch is giving a process gas flow reading above the 55.0 sccm upper limit.
Gas supply pressure is out of range.
A gas line valve is not fully open or is not in the correct position.
This looks like a first occurrence. ETCH-09 has no alarm or repair history in 90 days, and no other tool has reported A-1042 in 30 days. That makes a systemic or repeat cause less likely.

likely_causes: Showerhead holes are clogged, which gives uneven gas distribution and non-uniform film thickness.
The wafer is off-center on the heater, which gives uneven thickness across the wafer.
There is no recent alarm or repair history on this tool and no D-2048 on other tools, so this looks like an isolated event on DEP-06 chamber B. It does not look like a fleet-wide issue.

alarm_summary.recent_fix: No repairs recorded on CMP-08 in the last 30 days.

C-3005 has appeared on CMP-06 chamber A twice in the last 30 days (2026-11-08 and 2026-11-13). This could be a shared issue, but nothing confirms it.

alarm_summary.recent_alarm: In the last 7 days CMP-08 alarmed on C-3033 (chamber A, 11-15), C-3009 (chamber B, 11-16), C-3037 (chamber A, 11-17 08:30) and C-3005 (chamber A, 11-17 12:30). The 30-day history shows no other CMP-08 alarms.

likely_causes: Head down force is over the upper limit (5.1 psi against 2.0 to 4.0 psi). This could be a head air supply pressure or regulator problem.

alarm_summary.recent_alarm: CMP-06 alarmed repeatedly in the last 7 days, mostly on chamber A: C-3005 (2026-11-13, chamber A), C-3016 (2026-11-13, chamber B), C-3028 (2026-11-14, chamber A) and C-3041 (2026-11-16, chamber A). likely_causes: Slurry problem: wrong lot or expired slurry, which lowers the removal rate.
Worn pad: pad usage hours past their limit, which lowers the removal rate.

Possible tool-level issue: CMP-06 has had several different alarms in 4 days, and C-3005 came back on chamber A after the head membrane replacement. This is not confirmed as related to the chamber B low removal rate.

likely_causes: Slurry buildup on the endpoint sensor window is preventing endpoint detection, so polish time is 141 s against an upper limit of 120 s.
Polish process drift for this recipe is giving longer polish times.
The earlier C-3012 (chamber A) and C-3021 (chamber B) alarms on CMP-02 may point to a related consumable or tool condition. This is not confirmed.
CMP-06 chamber A also reported C-3041 on 2026-11-16, so a shared cause such as slurry lot, pad or recipe is possible.
